text: alex: Heads up — our builder image publish job started failing intermittently when the registry replica in eu-west lags behind us-west. CI shows old SBOM referenced after a successful push :confused: maria: Ugh, saw that too. The publish job is two-step: build+push to primary, then async replicate. The SBOM gets attached as a manifest list item and replication occasionally loses that tag. alex: Example errors in the job: `WARN: manifest sha256:abc123 missing annotation com.redwood/sbom` then later `docker pull eu-west.registry/...:builder-202603-xyz -> manifest unknown` timothy: Is this the cosign rotation window or real replication delay? We rotated the cosign key last week, but signatures verify fine on primary. sneha: I reproduced locally by pulling the eu-west registry after a push and it served the image but `cosign verify` failed because the sbom annotation was missing from the copied manifest. That suggests replication doesn't preserve OCI annotations in some cases. maria: We should not rely on async replication for release-critical metadata. Suggest: make CI attach SBOM to the image tag (not just manifest list) and verify on the target registry before announcing CI success. alex: Agreed. Proposed quick fix: CI step after replication does `docker pull /: && cosign verify --key $COSIGN_KEY /: && ./tools/verify-sbom.sh` ci-bot: build-14982: push succeeded to us-west.registry, started replication to eu-west (job 14982-replicate) ops-bot: replication-monitor: 1 replication failure detected last 24h between us-west -> eu-west for repo infra/builder-images timothy: Longer term: update registry replication config to preserve annotations and/or use registry-level manifest-copy instead of re-pushing. Also think about adding integration test in premerge that talks to a replica-backed registry env. alex: Another wrinkle — base image auto-rotation caused a rebuild cascade yesterday. Several builder images triggered CVE scans which flagged a transient layer; SBOMs showed slightly different package ordering and that confused our regression tooling. sneha: That ordering diff is from non-deterministic npm dependency flattening in the base image build. We should pin the base image digest and add a reproducible lockfile step in the base build. maria: Can we gate base-image rotations behind a canary fleet? For Dedicated customers we want predictability, not surprise rebuilds. Maybe a `base-rotation` feature flag that creates a canary tag and waits 24h telemetry before full rollout. timothy: Also cost note: pushing identical layers multiple times across regions is expensive. Consider using cross-region replication (read-only) and ripping out re-push pattern in builder pipeline. alex: For immediate action items: 1) Add verification step post-replication in CI (short-term). 2) Pin base image digests in builder Dockerfiles (short-term). 3) Create ticket to change replication strategy to manifest-copy preserving annotations (long-term). 4) Add SBOM/annotation check to gitops gating so Helm release won't proceed without verified SBOM in target registry. maria: I'll open the PR for the CI verification step and add the `cosign verify` + `jq` SBOM annotation check. Pinging @sneha for the base-image pin PR. sneha: On it. Will also add a `--no-cache` reproducible build mode for base images to see if ordering stabilizes. ci-bot: build-14983: post-replication verification started (eu-west). alex: Bonus: add a prometheus metric `registry_replication_lag_seconds` and an alert when > 300s for infra/builder-images. Ops wants that before we add more async steps. ops-bot: pagerduty: alert policy "registry-replication-lag" created in staging, severity=warning timothy: Sounds good. Also let's document the rollback steps if a signed image disappears from replica: `1) hold releases, 2) re-push manifest with annotations, 3) re-run cosign sign` — put that in runbook. maria: I'll add to runbook and link PR in this thread when ready. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: alex: Thanks — small patch now, follow-ups for canary and replication config.
